entries.title: Liebherr R 9800
entries.description: An 800-tonne hydraulic mining excavator built to load the very largest haul trucks in a handful of passes, and one of the two or three largest hydraulic excavators ever put into series production.

entries.title: Caterpillar D11
entries.description: Caterpillar's largest production bulldozer, built to push more material per pass than any other dozer in its catalogue, almost exclusively in mining rather than general construction.

entries.title: Caterpillar 994K
entries.description: Caterpillar's largest wheel loader, built to load haul trucks directly rather than push or carry material any real distance — a specialist at one job, done at enormous scale.

entries.title: Caterpillar 24 Motor Grader
entries.description: The largest motor grader Caterpillar builds, sized specifically to maintain the wide haul roads inside a mine rather than the narrower roads a construction grader typically finishes.

entries.title: Caterpillar 797F
entries.description: The largest mechanical-drive haul truck Caterpillar builds — a 400-ton-payload truck powered by a single, enormous diesel engine rather than the diesel-electric drivetrains some rivals use at this size.

entries.title: Bucyrus-Erie 4250-W “Big Muskie”
entries.description: The largest walking dragline ever built — a single, one-off machine so large it needed its own specially built rail cars just to ship its components to the mine where it was assembled.

entries.title: TAKRAF Bagger 293
entries.description: A bucket wheel excavator recognised by Guinness World Records as the heaviest land vehicle ever built, and — tied with its near-sister Bagger 288 — the tallest.

entries.title: Komatsu P&H 4100XPC
entries.description: An ultra-class electric rope shovel purpose-built to load the very largest mining haul trucks, using cable and hoist mechanics that predate hydraulic excavators by decades.

entries.title: Bertha (Hitachi Zosen TBM)
entries.description: At 17.5 metres in diameter, the largest earth-pressure-balance tunnel boring machine ever built, bored beneath downtown Seattle to replace the Alaskan Way Viaduct.

entries.title: Sarens SGC-250 “Big Carl”
entries.description: A purpose-built ring crane with a 5,000-tonne maximum lifting capacity, currently the largest land-based crane in the world.

entries.title: Kalmar DCG330
entries.description: A heavy industrial forklift built for handling loaded shipping containers and other massive loads at ports and intermodal yards, at nearly ten times the capacity of a typical warehouse forklift.

entries.title: JCB 541-70
entries.description: A telescopic handler that combines a forklift's carrying capacity with a crane-like telescoping boom, reaching well beyond what any fixed-mast forklift could manage.

entries.title: John Deere X9 1100
entries.description: John Deere's flagship combine harvester, built around a twin-rotor threshing system specifically to keep pace with the widest headers and highest field speeds in modern grain harvesting.

entries.title: John Deere 9RX
entries.description: John Deere's largest row-crop tractor, running on four independent tracks instead of wheels to put record horsepower onto soft ground without compacting it.

entries.title: John Deere R4045
entries.description: A self-propelled sprayer built to cover wide swaths of cropland quickly and precisely, applying crop protection products through booms that can stretch well beyond a football field's width.

entries.title: Epiroc Pit Viper 351
entries.description: A rotary blasthole drill rig built to bore the deep, wide holes mines fill with explosives to fracture rock ahead of loading — one of the largest rotary drills in regular production.

entries.title: Ponsse Bear
entries.description: An eight-wheeled forest harvester built to fell, delimb, and cut trees to length in a single continuous operation, sized for the largest timber a wheeled harvester is asked to handle.

entries.title: Konecranes RTG
entries.description: A rubber-tyred gantry crane that straddles multiple lanes of stacked shipping containers, moving on its own tyres between container blocks rather than running on fixed rails.

entries.title: M1150 Assault Breacher Vehicle
entries.description: A U.S. military combat engineering vehicle built on the M1 Abrams tank chassis, purpose-designed to clear paths through minefields and obstacle belts ahead of advancing forces.

entries.title: Spartacus (Cutter Suction Dredger)
entries.description: The most powerful cutter suction dredger ever built, and the first in the world powered by LNG, engineered to cut through harder seabed material at greater depth than any dredger before it.

entries.title: Torque
entries.description: Torque is a twisting force — how hard something is being turned around an axis, rather than pushed in a straight line. It is the rotational equivalent of force, and it is the single number that decides whether an engine can turn a wheel, a bolt, or a bucket wheel the size of a building.

entries.title: Mechanical Advantage
entries.description: Mechanical advantage is the factor by which a machine multiplies an input force. A machine with a mechanical advantage of 20 turns 50 kg of push into 1,000 kg of usable force — at the cost of the input having to move 20 times farther or faster than the output.

entries.title: Gear Ratios
entries.description: A gear ratio is the number of teeth on the driven gear divided by the number of teeth on the driving gear. It tells you, in one number, how a gear pair changes rotational speed and torque as power passes through it.

entries.title: Planetary Gears
entries.description: A planetary (epicyclic) gearset arranges a central sun gear, several orbiting planet gears on a carrier, and an outer ring gear with internal teeth, all meshed together and sharing one axis. Fixing any one of the three members and driving another produces a different gear ratio from the same set of parts.

entries.title: Pascal's Law
entries.description: Pascal's Law states that pressure applied to a confined, incompressible fluid is transmitted equally, undiminished, in every direction throughout that fluid. It is the entire physical basis of hydraulic machinery.

entries.title: Hydraulic Cylinders
entries.description: A hydraulic cylinder is a tube, a piston, and a rod that turns fluid pressure directly into a straight-line push or pull. It is the most common actuator on any heavy machine built after about 1950, because it can deliver enormous force from a compact, sealed package with no gears at all.

entries.title: Four-Stroke Diesel Cycle
entries.description: The four-stroke diesel cycle is the sequence of intake, compression, power, and exhaust that a diesel engine's piston repeats to convert fuel into rotating torque. Unlike a petrol engine, it ignites fuel using heat from compression alone, with no spark plug.

entries.title: Torque Converters
entries.description: A torque converter connects an engine to a transmission with spinning fluid instead of a mechanical clutch plate. It transmits power smoothly through oil, and — unlike a simple fluid coupling — can actually multiply torque when the engine is spinning much faster than the output shaft.

entries.title: Final Drives & Differentials
entries.description: The final drive is the last gear reduction in a driveline, sitting right at the wheel hub or track sprocket, where the very highest torque and lowest speed in the whole machine are required. The differential, usually just upstream of it, allows the two output shafts to spin at different speeds — essential the moment the machine turns a corner.

entries.title: Bearings
entries.description: A bearing is the part of a machine designed to take the friction, so nothing more expensive around it has to. It supports a rotating or sliding component while letting it move with as little resistance and wear as possible.

entries.title: What Kind of Heavy Machine Are You?
entries.description: A ten-question personality quiz scored against all 20 machines.
